full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee J. This criminal petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated the 8th day of August, 2017 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.14097 of 2016 disposing of the Rule. 

 2. The facts, relevant for disposal of the instant civil petition for leave to appeal, arc that earlier the High Court Division while issuing the Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.14097 of 2016 filed under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure at the instance of the accused-respondent herein, Md. Azad alias Abul Kaiam Azad in connection with Companigonj Police Station Case No. 13 dated 30.03.2014 corresponding to G.R. No. 537 of 2014, under sections 506/302/34 of the Penal Code, granted ad-interim bail for a period of 3(three) months vide order dated 18.04.2016. Subsequently, on the prayer of the said accused, the period of ad-interim bail was extended by the High Court Division for a further period of 1(one) year from the date of expiry vide order dated 08.08.2016 i.e. with effect from 17.07.2016. 

 6. Having considering the said factual position, which is apparent on the face on record, the High Court Division vide order dated 30.05.2017 allowed the application for a direction to release the present accused-respondent forth with in connection with Sessions Case No.226 of 2016 arising out of Companigonj Police Station Case No.13 dated 30.03.2014 corresponding to G.R. No.537 of 2014 and at the same time, Ms. Jebunnahar Ayesha, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Noakhali, who is also holding the charge of District and Sessions Judge, Noakhali, was directed to show cause as to why a contempt proceeding should not be drawn against her for disregarding the order dated 08.08.2016 passed by and High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 14097 of 2016 and to give writ-ten explanation to that effect on or before 07.06.2017. 

 10. Mr. A. M. Aminuddin, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioner, submits that as per record, accused-Azad was granted ad-interim bail on 18.04.2016 by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.14097 of 2016 pursuant to which he was released from custody on 10.05.2016. He also submits that subsequently, the bail was extended for further period of 1(one) year vide Order dated 08.08.2016 subject to condition that "The Court below is at liberty to cancel the bail of the petitioner if privilege of bail is misused by him in accordance with law." He further submits that the learned Sessions Judge, Noakhali, framed charge on 27.04.2016 and fixed date on 15.06.2016 in presence of accusedAbul Kalam Azad, but he remained absent on 15.06.2016 without taking any steps whatsoever. On the next date, i.e. on 11.08.2016, his engaged lawyer filed an application seeking time stating that he had no knowledge about the date which was against the averments of the case record. He however submits that more-over, on that date, the prosecution filed hazira of witness, the application filed on behalf of the accused was misguiding and he remained absent for consecutive days, thus accused-Azad has clearly violated the privilege of bail; hence, the Sessions Judge, Noakhali cancelled his bail on 11.08.2016 after the date of extension of bail on 08.08.2016 and that thereafter, accused-Azad remained fugitive for two successive dates, on i.e. 24.08.2016 and 02.10.2016 and also that the two applications were filed on behalf of accused-Azad on 18.10.2016 wherein he prayed for bail by treating him "as show arrest" stating that he is in custody for about 40 days in connection with G.R. No.1205 of 2016 on the allegation that accused-Abul Kalam Azad along with others, killed Abu Sufian, a charge sheeted witness of the instant case on 04.08.2016 after securing bail. Thereafter, he submits that the Police after holding investigation submitted charge-sheet being No.89 dated 06.062017 against him and that with a view to mislead the High Court Division and obtain favourable order application dated 06.05.2017 was filed on behalf of accused Azad concealing all those facts and, thereby, succeeded to convince the High Court Division that the Sessions Judge (in-charge), Noakhali passed the order dated 22.02.2017 disregarding the order dated 08.08.2016 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.14097 of 2016 and to pass the order dated 30.05.2017 directing the Sessions Judge(in-charge), Noakhali to pass necessary order to release him from custody which are contrary to actual facts and position of the case and settled principles of law and thus managed to get an order directing Ms. Jebunnahar Ayesha, learned Additional Sessions Judge, Noakhali to show cause as to why a contempt proceeding should not be drawn against her for disregarding the order dated 08.08.2016 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.14097 of 2016 and as such, the order dated 08.08.2017 passed by the High Court Division is not sustainable in the eye of law. Mr. Amin next submits that there was no disregard of the order dated 08.08.2016 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.14097 of 2016 in the order dated 22.02.2017 passed by Ms. Jebunnahar Ayesha, learned Additional Sessions Judge, Noakhali in Sessions Case No.226 of 2016 as the bail of accused-Abul Kalam Azad has already been cancelled earlier on 11.08.2016 of clear misuse of the privilege of bail; thus the Order dated 08.08.2016 of the High 

 Court Division was not in force on 22.02.2017, the High Court Division failed to consider this aspect of the case which thus has committed serious miscarriage of justice and as such, the order dated 08.08.2017 passed by the High Court Division is not sustainable in the eye of law and liable to be set aside. He further submits that the High Court Division considered 05(five) criteria for having misused the privilege of bail out of which criteria No.1, 3 and 5 are available in the present case and thus cancellation of bail by the learned Sessions Judge, Noakhali, in the present case was in accordance with law, the High Court Division misconceived and misconstrued the said aspect of the case and thus committed serious miscarriage of justice and as such, the Order dated 08.08.2017 passed by the High Court Division is not sustainable in the eye of law and liable to be set aside. He further submits that the High Court Division considered 05(five) criteria for having misused the privilege of bail out of which criteria Nos.1, 3 and 5 are available in the present case and thus cancellation of bail by the learned Sessions Judge, Noakhali, in the present case was in accordance with law, the High Court Division misconceived and misconstrued the said aspect of the case and thus committed serious miscarriage of justice and as such, the order dated 08.08.2017 passed by the High Court Division is not maintainable in the eye of law and liable to be set aside. 

 14. This order of bail was extended by another Bench presided over by Farah Mahbub and Mahmudul Hoque, J.J. on 08.08.2016 for a further period of one year from the date of expiry under the same terms and conditions. The Sessions Judge, Noakhali framed charge on 27.04.2016 and fixed date on 15.06.2016 for trial in presence of accused Abul Kalam Azad (opposite party No.1), but he remained absent on 15.06.2016 without taking any steps and thereafter, on next date, i.e. 11.08.2016, his engage lawyer who filed an application seeking time stating that he had no knowledge about the date which appears to be against the case record, but on that date prosecution filed hazira of witness, as the application file on behalf of the accused was misguiding and he remained absent for consecutive days, thus accused-Azad has clearly violated the privilege of bail and hence, the Sessions Judge, Noakhali cancel his bail on 11.08.2016 after date of extension of bail dated 08.08.2016. It also appears that thereafter accused-Azad remained fugitive for two successive dates, i.e. on 24.08.2016, 02.10.2016. It is evident that two applications were filed on behalf of accused-Azad on 18.10.2016 to put up file and praying for bail by treating him as being shown arrest stating that he is in custody for about 40 days in connection with GR No.1205 of 2016. It is to be mentioned here that accused-Abul Kalam Azad with others alleged to have been killed Abu Sufian, a charge sheeted witness of the instant case on 04.08.2c: , after securing bail, police after investigation submitted charge sheet being No.89 dated 06.06.2017 against him. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the contempt nor-petitioner argued that opposite party No. 1 obtained the order of bail on misguiding and misleading the High Court Division and thereby to obtain fovourable order dated 06.05.2017 was filed on behalf of accused-Azad concealing all these facts and thereby succeeded to believe the High Court Division that the Sessions Judge(in-charge), Noakhali passed the order dated 22.02.2017 disregarding the order dated 08.08.2016 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.14097 of 2016 and to pass order dated 30.05.2017. 

 15. From the written explanation furnished by the present petitioner (contemnor), it appears that accused-Md. Azad @ Abul Kalam Azad was fugitive since he failed to appear before the trial Court for consecutive two fixed dates, thereby, he had misused the privilege of bail and in the meantime, the case had been fixed for holding trial. It also appears that due to absence of the accused concerned, the trial Court declared him fugitive and also ordered to proceed with the case in absentia. Since the High Court Division while enlarging the accused on bail, allowed the trial Court to cancel the bail order in case of any misuse of privilege of bail, the contemptnor rightly exercised its power of cancelling the order of bail on this score of the trial as has been argued by the learned Advocate on behalf of the contemptnor. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent (with the leave of the Court) submits that the petitioner (contemptnor) committed the act of contempt by violating the Court's order and refused opposite party No.1(accused) to enlarge him on bail in spite of standing order of the High Court Division and thereby will-fully and deliberately flouted the Court's order. Now the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the contemptnor argued that there is no willful or deliberate disregard of the Courts order and no contempt what so ever has been committed the petitioner (contemptnor). 

 16. Having considered the facts, circumstances of the case, it appears that the trial Court has not isolated the order of the High Court Division. Sometimes, it seems that in course of trial, the enlarged accused on bail, taking opportunity of privilege of bail creates obstructions in different ways with a view to delay the trial of the case as has been occurred in the instant case. In the present one, we have observed that incompliance with the processes of the Court, the witness remained present in the Court room for their examination, but the accused remained absent on the plea that he is being granted bail from the High Court Division. In such a situation, the trial Court since issued the process earlier for ensuring the attendance of the witness, felt embarrass. Having considered such circumstances, the trial Court has no other alternative but to cancel the bail order of the accused concerned and declare him to be a fugitive with a view to hold the trial in absentia. Perhaps keeping in mind to overcome such situation, the High Court Division allowed the liberty to the trial Court to cancel the order of bail in case of any misuse. 

 17. Here it may not be out of place to refer to the observations of Sir George Jessel, Master of the Rolls, in the case in re: Clements, Republic of Costa Rica Vs Eglanger (1876 46LJCJ375 383). He observed: 

 18. In view of the facts and circumstances discussed hereinbefore, it is difficult to say that the present petitioner has disrespected the order of the High Court Division deliberately and willfully, especially, when the circumstances and procedure to hold the trial in absentia requires cancelling the bail order and declaring the accused concerned to be a fugitive. Every infraction of the Court's order does not amount contempt of Court. It is only a willful and deliberate isolation of the Court's order and contumacious conduct on the part of the contemnor. A mere breach of the order is not contempt. It must amount to disdainful disregard of process of justice. We, therefore, find nothing in the instant case which tantamounts to disdainful disregard of the Court's order or a contumacious conduct on the part of the petitioner.
